info.disabled: When blank: alerts are delivered by email only.
info.risk: The URL is itself a credential -- anyone who has it can post into that channel -- so only Admins can see it. Alert details (account names, groups, roles) leave your environment to that endpoint. Alerts raised by the scheduled engine job are mailed but not posted to the webhook. Reversible: clear the URL and save.
info.requires: Admin role in PIM Manager. Outbound HTTPS from the PIM Manager to the endpoint. The 'Teams / webhook alerting' feature switch (Feature customization, on by default) must be on: switched off, nothing is posted even with a URL saved.
info.recommended: Use a Teams channel your operations team watches, alongside email recipients, so failures are seen even if mail stops.

info.what: The shape of what is posted to the outbound webhook. Microsoft Teams posts a message card with a colour by severity, the alert facts and an Open PIM Manager button. Generic JSON posts a flat object with event, title, detail, severity, tenant, link and time, for a Logic App or your own receiver.
info.enabled: When set to Microsoft Teams: the next alert is posted as a Teams message card.
info.disabled: At the default (Generic JSON): the next alert is posted as a flat JSON object. A Teams webhook given Generic JSON may show the raw text or reject it.
info.risk: Low. A format the endpoint does not understand makes the post fail; the failure shows in Recent alerts. Reversible at any time.
info.requires: Admin role in PIM Manager. An outbound webhook URL.
info.recommended: Microsoft Teams for a Teams incoming webhook; Generic JSON for anything else.

info.what: The longest activation PIM Manager lets any policy template recommend, picked from 1 hour to 3 days. It caps the PIM Manager recommendation for the groups and roles PIM Manager manages: a template whose 'An activation lasts at most' is longer is recommended at this value instead. A template that is already shorter is left as it is. It is part of the recommendation only: PIM Manager never changes a policy on its own.
info.enabled: When set lower than a template: the recommendation shown on Templates > Policy settings is shortened to this value. A policy is shortened in Entra only where a SuperAdmin chose 'PIM Manager recommendation' for 'Longest activation', and that change set is held until a SuperAdmin approves it (Reviews & controls > Approvals) -- whatever its size. The engine log names each template it shortened.
info.disabled: At the default (1 day): nothing changes -- Entra itself allows at most 24 hours for an activation, so the default never shortens a template.
info.risk: Medium when you lower it: where 'PIM Manager recommendation' is chosen and the change is approved, people who activate for longer than the new value have to activate again sooner. Activations already running are not cut short. Reversible: pick a longer value and save; the recommendation is the template's own value again.
info.requires: SuperAdmin to change it. Free (Community) and Pro. Applies only to groups and roles PIM Manager manages.
info.recommended: Leave it at 1 day and set the activation length per template; lower it to enforce a maximum across every template.

info.what: The longest eligible assignment PIM Manager lets a policy template allow (30, 90, 180 or 365 days). The engine applies it to the policies it writes for the groups and roles PIM Manager manages, where the template requires an eligibility to end: a longer maximum is shortened to this value. A template that allows a permanent eligibility keeps it.
info.enabled: When set lower than a template: on the next engine run Entra is told that new eligible assignments under that template may last at most this long. The engine log names each template it shortened.
info.disabled: At the default (365 days): nothing changes -- 365 days is also the longest the shipped templates allow.
info.risk: Medium when you lower it: new or renewed eligibilities end sooner, so people need them renewed more often. Eligibilities that exist today are not shortened. Reversible: pick a longer value and save.
info.requires: SuperAdmin to change it. Free (Community) and Pro. Applies only to groups and roles PIM Manager manages.
info.recommended: Leave it at 365 days unless your policy demands shorter eligibility everywhere.

on.title: Require MFA when someone activates?
on.body: When on, people must complete MFA when they activate a role or group that PIM Manager manages.

info.what: A floor on every activation policy the engine writes for the groups and roles PIM Manager manages. When it is on, the engine adds MFA to the 'To activate, require' checks of any policy template that sets those checks without MFA (a template that asks for a Conditional Access authentication context counts as covered). It never removes a check a template asks for.
info.enabled: When on: on the next engine run every managed group and role whose template sets activation checks without MFA requires MFA when someone activates, through the normal policy apply and its safety checks. A template that sets no activation checks at all is reported in the engine log and left to Entra.
info.disabled: When off: the engine applies the activation checks exactly as each policy template says -- a template without MFA then activates without MFA. Turning it off does not by itself remove MFA anywhere: the shipped templates all require MFA.
info.risk: Low when on (people must complete MFA when they activate). Turning it off removes the safety net for a template that forgets MFA. Reversible at any time; the next engine run applies the new value.
info.requires: SuperAdmin to change it. Free (Community) and Pro. Applies only to groups and roles PIM Manager manages.
info.recommended: Keep it on.

settings.label: Workload exemptions
settings.where: Settings > Hybrid AD & workloads > Workload exemptions

info.what: A list of workload role bindings (for example a Defender XDR or Intune role for a group) that you deliberately do not want created. Each entry names a workload and/or a role, optionally a group tag and a scope, a reason, and an expiry date or No expiry. A blank group tag or scope means 'any'.
info.enabled: When an entry is active: the workload reconciliation shows the binding as 'exempted' instead of 'missing', and on its next run the engine's workload connector reports it and does not create it. It never removes a binding that already exists. The day after the expiry date the exemption stops counting, the binding shows as missing again and the next run creates it.
info.disabled: When the list is empty: every desired workload binding is expected to exist, and the engine creates any that are missing on its next run.
info.risk: An entry with only a workload (no role) excuses every role of that workload. Removing an entry, or letting it expire, lets the engine create that role assignment in your tenant on its next run. Only the generic workload connector honours exemptions; a Defender XDR row that carries its own custom role definition is applied by a separate step that does not read this list. Reversible: add or remove entries at any time.
info.requires: Admin to add or remove entries; anyone can read them. Free (Community) and Pro. Takes effect only where the workload connectors are on and the engine has the workload's own permissions.
info.recommended: Use it sparingly, always with a real reason and an expiry date, so an exemption is reviewed instead of becoming permanent.

settings.label: Keep configuration backups for (days)
settings.where: Operations > Backups & restore (also Settings > Copy & tools > Configuration backups)

on.title: Keep configuration backups for fewer days?
on.body: Backups older than this are deleted at the next daily run.
on.note: Tip: pin any backup you must keep before you save.

info.what: How many days PIM Manager keeps its daily configuration backups (departments, external companies, admins, group definitions, delegations, workload bindings and settings -- never secrets). Any whole number from 1 to 3650.
info.enabled: When set: once a day the backup job takes a backup (or records 'no change') and then deletes every backup older than this many days. Pinned backups are always kept, the newest real backup is always kept so there is a restore point, and a backup a kept 'no change' record points to is kept. Each prune is written to the audit trail.
info.disabled: At the default (90 days): the same daily prune, with a 90-day window.
info.risk: Lowering the value deletes older backups permanently at the next daily run -- they cannot be restored afterwards. Pin any backup you must keep before you lower it. Raising it keeps more backups (more database space). Reversible for the future only: a higher value does not bring back backups already pruned.
info.requires: SuperAdmin to change it; Admin can read it. Free (Community) and Pro. The daily config-backup job must be enabled (it is by default).
info.recommended: Keep 90 days or more, and pin a backup before any large change you may want to roll back.

on.title: Delete old audit history?
on.body: Audit history older than this is deleted every day and cannot be brought back.
on.note: Tip: check your own retention rules before you save.

info.what: How long the audit trail keeps its rows. 0 keeps every row forever. Any other value must be 13 to 1200 months. Audit rows can never be edited, and the database itself refuses any delete that does not come from the retention job.
info.enabled: When set (13 months or more): the daily audit-retention job deletes the audit rows older than that, at most 50,000 per run (the rest on the following runs), and records each run -- cutoff, rows deleted, rows left -- as a new event in the audit trail.
info.disabled: At 0 (the default): the job runs and deletes nothing. Every audit row is kept.
info.risk: Deleted audit rows are gone for good: evidence for an investigation or a compliance review older than the window is lost. Check your own retention obligations first. Reversible for the future only: setting it back to 0 stops further deletes but does not restore deleted rows.
info.requires: SuperAdmin to change it; Admin can read it. Free (Community) and Pro. The daily audit-retention job must be enabled (it is by default).
info.recommended: Keep every row (0) unless a policy requires a limit; if you set one, use at least the period your auditors expect, for example 24 months or more.

settings.label: Extend ... days before a permission ends

info.what: How many days before a time-bound assignment ends the engine renews it (1 to 90). It applies to every expiring delegation PIM manages: group memberships of admins, nested groups, Entra role, administrative-unit and Azure role assignments that are set to auto-extend.
info.enabled: When set: on each engine run, an assignment that ends within this many days and is allowed to extend is renewed for the row's number of days, counted from that run. The 'Upcoming automatic extensions' list and the monthly owner mail show the date each one will be extended. Takes effect on the next engine run.
info.disabled: At the default (14 days): assignments are renewed 14 days before they end.
info.risk: Too short a lead time leaves little room if an engine run fails, so access can lapse. A long lead time renews earlier and gives owners less time to deny. Reversible: change it; the next run uses the new value.
info.requires: SuperAdmin to change it. Free (Community) and Pro. The engine needs the same rights it uses to create the assignments (for example RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory).
info.recommended: Keep 14 days: enough margin for a failed run, and owners still get their monthly list to deny what should end.

settings.label: Rows without an AutoExtend value are extended

off.title: Stop renewing access by default?
off.body: When off, access that has no renewal choice of its own ends on its end date.
off.note: Note: many people can lose access on their end dates without anyone acting.

info.what: What a blank AutoExtend cell on a delegation row means. Who decides an extension, first match wins: an access review outcome (Keep extends, Remove does not), then an owner's Deny of that exact end date, then the row's own TRUE / FALSE, and only then this default.
info.enabled: When on: a row with a blank AutoExtend value is renewed by the engine before it ends, like a row set to TRUE, unless a review or an owner says otherwise. Silence means extend.
info.disabled: When off: a row with a blank AutoExtend value is NOT renewed. On its end date the membership or role assignment simply ends in your tenant, and the person loses that access.
info.risk: Switching it off can make many people lose access on their end dates without anyone acting -- every row created without an explicit AutoExtend value is affected. Reversible: switch it back on; the next engine run renews what is still live, but an assignment that already ended is only recreated by the engine's normal reconcile of the row.
info.requires: SuperAdmin to change it. Free (Community) and Pro. Works together with the lead time above and with access reviews and owner decisions on the same page.
info.recommended: Keep it on, and use explicit AutoExtend=FALSE on rows (or an owner Deny) for access that must end.

off.title: Save changes without a second approver?
off.body: When off, the person who prepared a change can also save it.
off.note: Note: this removes the four-eyes check on your configuration.

info.what: Whether a change must be committed by a different administrator than the one who staged it. Off: anyone may commit what they staged. Sensitive: changes classed as sensitive (a privileged role or scope added to a group, a guest put into a privileged group, a disable or offboarding) need a second person. All: every change does.
info.enabled: When set to Sensitive or All: a commit that carries out a change you staged yourself -- or, under All, any direct edit you make -- is refused with 'a second administrator must commit this', and the refusal is audited. Another administrator opens the shared queue and commits it. Applies from the next commit.
info.disabled: When Off (the default): the person who staged a change may commit it. Rows staged by a colleague stay locked to them in every mode.
info.risk: With only one administrator, Sensitive or All blocks that person's own commits. Note that a SuperAdmin can switch the mode back to Off alone. Turning it Off removes the four-eyes check on your configuration. Reversible at any time.
info.requires: SuperAdmin to change it. Free (Community) and Pro. Needs at least two people with the Admin or SuperAdmin role.
info.recommended: Sensitive, when you have two or more administrators: privileged changes get a second pair of eyes without slowing everyday edits.

off.title: Let one SuperAdmin release a hold alone?
off.body: When off, one SuperAdmin can release a held run alone, after giving a reason.
off.note: Note: this removes the second-person check on large removals.

info.what: Whether releasing a safety guard needs a second SuperAdmin. A release lets one held engine plan through for one run or until a time (at most 24 hours) -- for example more removals than the per-run removal budget, or more account disables than the circuit breaker allows.
info.enabled: When on: a new release is created as pending. The engine will not use it until a different SuperAdmin approves it on the Guards page. The person who created it cannot approve it. The same holds for an approval of removals given in the commit popup: the engine uses it only after a different SuperAdmin approved it on the Guards page. If the setting cannot be read, PIM Manager treats it as on.
info.disabled: When off (the default): one SuperAdmin with a reason of at least 10 characters releases a guard alone, and the next matching engine run may use it.
info.risk: Off means a single SuperAdmin can let the engine remove or disable more than the guards normally allow in one run. The switch itself can be turned off by one SuperAdmin. Releases are always audited and bound to the exact plan; a changed plan is held again. Reversible at any time; a release already pending stays pending.
info.requires: SuperAdmin to change it. Free (Community) and Pro. Needs at least two SuperAdmins when on.
info.recommended: On, when you have two or more SuperAdmins: a release can remove access at scale, so it deserves a second pair of eyes.

settings.label: Limit: commit removal check
settings.default: 25 rows of one list in one commit

info.what: How many rows of one list a single commit may take out before a SuperAdmin has to approve it. It is a count: there is no share of the list in the rule, so taking 2 rows out of a list of 3 does not ask, and taking 26 rows out of a list of 1000 does. Two more cases always ask, whatever this number is, and their numbers are fixed: a commit that keeps none of the rows the list has now (also when it adds new ones), and a commit that would leave 2 rows or fewer of a list that has more than 5 rows.
info.enabled: When set: a commit that takes more rows than this out of one list is not saved. The commit popup shows the rows and the two numbers. An Admin reads that a SuperAdmin must approve; a SuperAdmin gets an Approve button and must give a reason. The approval covers exactly the rows shown and is recorded with who, when, why and every row.
info.disabled: At the default: 25 rows. The check itself cannot be switched off.
info.risk: A higher number lets an Admin remove more rows of a list in one commit without a second pair of eyes. A lower number asks a SuperAdmin more often. The number can only be set from 5 to 200; a stored value outside that range is ignored and 25 applies. Reversible at any time.
info.requires: SuperAdmin to change it, on Operations > Guards. Free (Community) and Pro.
info.recommended: Keep 25 unless routine clean-ups in your lists are larger. Raise it for a planned bulk change rather than permanently, or let a SuperAdmin approve that one commit.

info.what: How many removals one engine run may apply in one scope without an approval. When a run would remove more, it removes none of them in that scope and holds the list. This ONE number bounds seven things: removals a row asks for (Action = Remove), per kind of assignment; the clean-up of leftovers PIM Manager manages (a full run with prune); removals by the daily reconcile, where it is set to enforce; groups deleted because their definition is marked Retire; groups deleted from the change queue (a DELETE chosen on the Drift page); admin accounts offboarded in one run; and, in a managed tenant, central admins the managing tenant withdraws in one pull. Raising it raises all seven.
info.enabled: When set: up to this many removals per scope are applied by a run without asking. More than this needs a SuperAdmin's approval of the exact list: in the commit popup when the removals are committed (the run then applies exactly those items, whatever their number), or on Operations > Guards for a list a run already holds. Anything that is not in the approved list is still held.
info.disabled: At the default: 5 removals per scope per run. The guard itself cannot be switched off.
info.risk: A higher number lets one run remove more access without anyone approving the list: a wrong bulk edit or a bad read does more damage before it is noticed. The number can only be set from 1 to 25; a stored value outside that range is ignored and 5 applies. Reversible at any time.
info.requires: SuperAdmin to change it, on Operations > Guards. Free (Community) and Pro.
info.recommended: Keep 5. For a planned clean-up, let a SuperAdmin approve that list when it is committed instead of raising the limit for every run.

info.what: How many admin accounts one engine run may disable. It is a count of accounts: the share of the scanned accounts plays no part. When a run would disable more, it disables none of them and holds the list. The number bounds three things: accounts disabled because their row says so (the account status, a passed disable date), accounts disabled by an offboarding in one run, and accounts disabled by the inactivity sweep where it is set to enforce.
info.enabled: When set: up to this many accounts are disabled by a run when their rows say so. More than this is held until a SuperAdmin releases exactly that list of accounts on Operations > Guards, for one run. Break-glass accounts are never disabled, whatever this number is.
info.disabled: At the default: 3 accounts per run. The breaker itself cannot be switched off.
info.risk: A higher number lets one run lock more administrators out before anyone has looked at the list. The number can only be set from 1 to 25; a stored value outside that range is ignored and 3 applies. Reversible at any time.
info.requires: SuperAdmin to change it, on Operations > Guards. Free (Community) and Pro.
info.recommended: Keep 3: a real offboarding is a few accounts. For a larger one, release that exact list once instead of raising the limit.

info.what: How many assignments one bulk revoke may take away before it needs more than a click. A batch larger than this must be confirmed by typing its exact count, and it needs an approved request on the Approvals page. Both checks use this one number.
info.enabled: When set: a revoke of up to this many assignments goes ahead after the usual confirmation. A larger batch is confirmed with its count and approved by a person with permission over the assignments (their scope and level) or a SuperAdmin -- never by the person who asked.
info.disabled: At the default: 5 assignments in one batch. The check itself cannot be switched off.
info.risk: A higher number lets one person revoke more access in one batch without a second person. The number can only be set from 1 to 25; a stored value outside that range is ignored and 5 applies. Reversible at any time.
info.requires: SuperAdmin to change it, on Operations > Guards. Free (Community) and Pro.
info.recommended: Keep 5. For a planned larger revoke, have it approved once instead of raising the limit.

settings.label: Limit: admin account deletes per run

info.what: How many admin accounts one engine run may delete. An account is deleted only when its row says Deleted, which was approved before it was stored. When more accounts are waiting, the rest are deleted by the next run.
info.enabled: When set: up to this many approved account deletes are carried out per run; the others wait for the next run. Break-glass accounts are never deleted, whatever this number is.
info.disabled: At the default: 5 account deletes per run. The limit itself cannot be switched off.
info.risk: A higher number deletes more accounts in one run. A deleted account can be restored from the directory's deleted users for 30 days. The number can only be set from 1 to 25; a stored value outside that range is ignored and 5 applies. Reversible at any time.
info.requires: SuperAdmin to change it, on Operations > Guards. Free (Community) and Pro.
info.recommended: Keep 5.

settings.label: Reminders: what waits on you
settings.where: Settings > Mail & alerting > Reminders: what waits on you
settings.default: On -- first reminder after 4 hours for an approval and 24 hours for a Get Started step, then every 24 hours

off.title: Stop reminder mail?
off.body: When off, nobody is reminded by mail about changes or requests that wait for them.
off.note: Note: held work can then wait without anyone noticing.

info.what: Whether PIM Manager mails your SuperAdmins when something waits on them: open required Get Started steps, policy change sets held by the circuit breaker, approval and access requests, guard holds and releases, a break-glass change, and staged changes a second administrator must commit. One mail lists everything, each item with a link to the exact place where you act. It is sent by your own PIM Manager, not by Invardia.
info.enabled: When on (the default): the first reminder goes out when an approval has waited the set number of hours (default 4) or a Get Started step has been open that long (default 24), then it repeats every set number of hours (default 24) while anything waits. It stops by itself when nothing waits. Alert recipients who are not SuperAdmins get the Get Started part. Each person can switch either part off for themselves under Notifications.
info.disabled: When off: no reminder is sent. Held changes, requests and open Get Started steps still show on the Home page and their own pages, but nobody is told by mail.
info.risk: Off means a held change set, a guard hold or an access request can wait unnoticed, and the engine skips what is held until someone acts. Very short hours mean more mail. Reversible at any time; the next scheduler run uses the new values.
info.requires: Admin or SuperAdmin to change it. Free (Community) and Pro. A mail sender must be set up (Settings > Mail & alerting > Mail sending); while mail is muted or no sender is set, the reminder is recorded but not delivered.
info.recommended: On, with the defaults. Lower the approval hours if people wait on approvals during the working day.

settings.label: Break-glass accounts
settings.where: Settings > Emergency access (break-glass); also Get Started > Break-glass

on.title: Protect your emergency accounts?
on.body: PIM Manager will never change, disable or sign out the accounts on this list.
on.note: Tip: only add your real emergency (break-glass) accounts.
more: A change to the list needs approval, and applies from the next run after it is approved.
If the list cannot be read, PIM Manager removes nothing at all in that run.
You can take an account off the list again with a new approved request.

off.title: Stop protecting these emergency accounts?
off.body: Accounts you take off the list can be changed, disabled or signed out by PIM Manager again.
off.note: Note: only do this for accounts that are no longer emergency accounts.
more: A change to the list needs approval, and applies from the next run after it is approved.
When the list is empty, no account is protected this way.

info.what: The emergency accounts PIM must never lock out, by sign-in name (UPN) or object id. Both PIM Manager and the engine read this one list. A change is not applied directly: it becomes a request that a different SuperAdmin must approve within 72 hours, and every step is audited.
info.enabled: When an account is on the list: every revoke, disable, sign-in session revoke and offboarding path in PIM skips it -- the engine, queued actions, access reviews and the disable circuit breaker. From the engine's next run after the request is approved.
info.disabled: When the list is empty: no account is exempt, so PIM can revoke, disable or offboard any account its rules reach -- including your emergency accounts.
info.risk: Adding an account shields it from every PIM guard, so only list real emergency accounts. Removing one makes it reachable by PIM's removals again. If the list cannot be read, PIM treats every account as break-glass and removes nothing that run. Reversible through a new approved request.
info.requires: SuperAdmin to request a change, and a second, different SuperAdmin to approve it. Free (Community) and Pro.
info.recommended: List your two or more cloud-only emergency accounts by UPN, and keep them out of every PIM group.

settings.label: PIM Activator deployment groups (PROD / TEST) and additional tenants
settings.default: No group for PROD or TEST; no additional tenants

info.what: The group that gets the PIM Activator browser extension deployed, one for PROD and one for TEST, picked from your directory, plus an optional list of extra tenants for the extension's catalog. It is about deployment only -- which devices or users Intune and Edge for Business send the extension and its settings to. It does not decide who may sign in to the PIM Activator: what a person can activate is decided by their PIM eligibility. PIM Manager writes nothing to your tenant here: the values are filled into the ready-made commands and the guide on the page.
info.enabled: When a group is set: the Intune command for that channel assigns the settings to that group (and only that group), and the Edge for Business guide names it as the group to assign the policy to. The group is checked in your directory before it is saved. Extra tenants are validated and added to the commands' catalog.
info.disabled: When blank (the default): the Intune command assigns the settings to nobody and says so, and the Edge for Business guide asks you to choose a group. Never all users or all devices.
info.risk: A too-broad group puts the extension on more devices than you meant once an admin runs the command; it gives nobody more access. Changing the group only changes the command text; what is already assigned in Intune or Edge for Business stays until you change it there. Reversible: pick another group or clear it.
info.requires: Admin to change it. The Manager needs to read groups in your directory to confirm the group. Running the Intune command needs an Intune Administrator.
info.recommended: Use a dedicated group holding only your administrators, and a separate small group for TEST.

settings.label: Policy template used where a delegation names none -- PIM for Groups

on.title: Use another default policy template for PIM groups?
on.body: PIM Manager's recommendation for these groups then follows the template you chose.
on.note: Tip: no policy changes until a SuperAdmin approves the change.

info.what: The policy template that gives the PIM Manager recommendation for the PIM for Groups policy of every group PIM Manager manages whose definition leaves the policy template blank. A template recommends how long an activation lasts, what is required to activate (for example multifactor authentication, a reason) and whether approval is needed. It is a recommendation only: PIM Manager never changes a policy on its own.
info.enabled: When set: the recommendation shown for these groups on Templates > Policy settings follows the chosen template. A policy changes only for the settings where a SuperAdmin chose 'PIM Manager recommendation'. Every change set that comes from a choice is held, whatever its size, and nothing is written until it is approved. A SuperAdmin of the tenant approves the held change set in PIM Manager (Reviews & controls > Approvals); the approval is valid for 24 hours. The held change set says how many policies change and how many settings are weakened, and points out when more than 25 policies change or more than 3 settings are weakened (fixed numbers, not a setting: they never decide whether a change set is held).
info.disabled: At the built-in default: the recommendation for these groups comes from Groups_Standard.
info.risk: Picking another template changes what 'PIM Manager recommendation' means for many groups at once. Where that choice is made, the next policy run plans the change and holds it for a SuperAdmin's approval; settings on 'Keep current' or 'Microsoft default' are not affected. Reversible: pick the previous template.
info.requires: SuperAdmin to change it. Free (Community) and Pro. The template must exist and be written for PIM for Groups. The engine needs RoleManagementPolicy.ReadWrite.AzureADGroup.
info.recommended: Keep the built-in default unless your organisation has its own group standard; name a template on the definitions that need stricter rules. Then choose per setting on Templates > Policy settings.

settings.label: Policy template used where a delegation names none -- Entra ID roles

on.title: Use another default policy template for Entra ID roles?
on.body: PIM Manager's recommendation for these roles then follows the template you chose.
on.note: Note: a role's policy applies to everyone who holds that role, and nothing changes until a SuperAdmin approves.

info.what: The policy template that gives the PIM Manager recommendation for the Entra ID role policy of every role your delegations assign (to groups, in administrative units, or directly) when the row leaves the policy template blank. If two rows name the same role with different templates, the one requiring approval wins. It is a recommendation only: PIM Manager never changes a policy on its own.
info.enabled: When set: the recommendation shown for these roles on Templates > Policy settings follows the chosen template. A role's policy changes only for the settings where a SuperAdmin chose 'PIM Manager recommendation'. Every change set that comes from a choice is held, whatever its size, and nothing is written until it is approved. A SuperAdmin of the tenant approves the held change set in PIM Manager (Reviews & controls > Approvals); the approval is valid for 24 hours. The held change set says how many policies change and how many settings are weakened, and points out when more than 25 policies change or more than 3 settings are weakened (fixed numbers, not a setting: they never decide whether a change set is held).
info.disabled: At the built-in default: the recommendation for these roles comes from EntraIDRoles_Standard.
info.risk: A role policy applies to everyone who holds that role in the tenant, not only the groups PIM Manager manages. Picking another template changes what 'PIM Manager recommendation' means for all of them; where that choice is made, the next policy run plans the change and holds it for a SuperAdmin's approval. Reversible: pick the previous template.
info.requires: SuperAdmin to change it. Free (Community) and Pro. The template must exist and be written for Entra ID roles. The engine needs RoleManagementPolicy.ReadWrite.Directory.
info.recommended: Keep the built-in default, and name an approval-required template on the rows for your most privileged roles. Then choose per setting on Templates > Policy settings.

settings.label: Policy template used where a delegation names none -- Azure resource roles

on.title: Use another default policy template for Azure roles?
on.body: PIM Manager's recommendation for these Azure roles then follows the template you chose.
on.note: Note: an Azure role's policy applies to everyone eligible for it, and nothing changes until a SuperAdmin approves.

info.what: The policy template that gives the PIM Manager recommendation for the PIM policy of each Azure role and scope pair your Azure delegations assign when the row leaves the policy template blank. If two rows name the same pair with different templates, the one requiring approval wins. It is a recommendation only: PIM Manager never changes a policy on its own.
info.enabled: When set: the recommendation shown for these Azure roles on Templates > Policy settings follows the chosen template. A policy changes only for the settings where a SuperAdmin chose 'PIM Manager recommendation'. Every change set that comes from a choice is held, whatever its size, and nothing is written until it is approved. A SuperAdmin of the tenant approves the held change set in PIM Manager (Reviews & controls > Approvals); the approval is valid for 24 hours. The held change set says how many policies change and how many settings are weakened, and points out when more than 25 policies change or more than 3 settings are weakened (fixed numbers, not a setting: they never decide whether a change set is held).
info.disabled: At the built-in default: the recommendation for these pairs comes from AzureRoles_Standard (the same rules as the Entra role standard).
info.risk: An Azure role policy applies to everyone eligible for that role on that scope. Picking another template changes what 'PIM Manager recommendation' means for all of them; where that choice is made, the next policy run plans the change and holds it for a SuperAdmin's approval. PIM Manager never switches approval off on an Azure role policy. Reversible: pick the previous template.
info.requires: SuperAdmin to change it. Free (Community) and Pro. The template must exist and be written for Azure resource roles. The engine's identity needs a role that may change role management policies on those scopes (for example User Access Administrator or Owner).
info.recommended: Keep the built-in default, and name an approval-required template on rows that grant Owner or User Access Administrator. Then choose per setting on Templates > Policy settings.

settings.label: Manage delegation / role mapping
settings.default: Empty (only the access granted at setup applies; every other signed-in user is a Reader)

on.title: Give these people more rights in PIM Manager?
on.body: The people and groups you mapped get their new PIM Manager role within seconds.
on.note: Tip: give Admin and SuperAdmin only to people who need them, because they can change admin access in your tenant.

info.what: Who may do what in PIM Manager: each sign-in name is mapped to Reader (view only), Delegated (view only, limited to the groups they own), Admin (stage, commit and revoke) or SuperAdmin (everything, including settings, emergency access and this map). Each entry is one person; groups are not expanded.
info.enabled: When saved: the server enforces the map on every request, within about 15 seconds. Saving is refused if no SuperAdmin would remain, and a new Delegated entry needs Pro. Without Pro, an existing Delegated entry acts as Reader.
info.disabled: For a person not in the map (and not granted at setup): PIM Manager still lets them in as a Reader if they can sign in, so they can view configuration and assignments but not change anything.
info.risk: Admin and SuperAdmin can change who holds privileged access in your tenant through the engine, so grant them only to people who need them. Removing someone takes effect within seconds. Reversible: edit the map again. Every save is audited.
info.requires: SuperAdmin to change it. Delegated entries need Pro; Reader, Admin and SuperAdmin are Free (Community). At least one SuperAdmin must remain.
info.recommended: Keep two SuperAdmins (so second-approver controls work), give everyday operators Admin, and limit who can sign in to PIM Manager at all with the app's user assignment.

settings.label: Automatic offboarding
settings.default: Not set: off in a production tenant, on in a tenant named as a test tenant

info.what: Decides whether the engine acts by itself on an admin account that is due for offboarding: its offboard date has passed, it is marked Retire, or its status is Revoked. The offboarding job (admin-offboarding) reads the switch at every run. The card shows the state in effect and where it comes from. PIM Manager asks for confirmation before the switch is changed, in either direction.
info.enabled: When on: from its next run the offboarding job disables such an account, signs it out everywhere, removes its group memberships and eligibilities and sends the offboarding notice. The account itself is never deleted.
info.disabled: When off: the offboarding job does nothing for these accounts. The group memberships and eligibilities such an account holds stay until the switch is on or somebody removes them by hand.
info.risk: On: access is removed without a person looking at each account, so a wrong offboard date or a wrong Retire mark takes a working administrator's access away. The account-disable guard still applies and cannot be switched off here. Off: an account that should have lost its access keeps it. Switching off later does not put removed access back.
info.requires: SuperAdmin to change it, with a confirmation. A setting made in the engine job's own environment wins over this switch; the card says so where PIM Manager can read it.
info.recommended: On once your offboard dates are maintained and you have checked, on Jobs, which accounts the offboarding job lists. Off while you are still cleaning up dates.

settings.label: Daily reconcile: removal of leftovers
settings.where: Settings > Approvals & policy > Daily reconcile: removal of leftovers

info.what: Decides what the daily full run (the job full-reconcile) does with a leftover: a live assignment or membership that PIM Manager put in your tenant, whose definition was later removed by a PIM Manager commit, and for which nothing similar is configured. The card shows the mode in effect, where it comes from and what the last daily run counted. PIM Manager asks for confirmation before the mode is changed.
info.enabled: When set to 'Remove leftovers': the daily run removes the leftovers that qualify. It never disables or deletes an admin account, never removes a shared Defender XDR or Intune assignment, and never removes anything that existed before PIM Manager recorded its changes.
info.disabled: When set to 'Report only': the daily run removes none of them and lists on Jobs what it would remove. Not set at all means 'Remove leftovers'.
info.risk: Remove leftovers: a removal cannot be undone from this page; the removal guard still applies and cannot be switched off here, and when more items qualify than the guard allows in one run, none is removed in that run. Report only: access whose definition was removed stays live in your tenant until somebody removes it by hand.
info.requires: SuperAdmin to change it, with a confirmation. While nothing is set here, a value in the engine job's own environment decides; the card says so where PIM Manager can read it.
info.recommended: Remove leftovers, so that removing a definition also removes the access. Use Report only while you investigate what a run would remove, then set it back.

settings.label: An approval request expires after (hours)
settings.where: Settings > Approvals & policy > Approval and request limits

info.what: How long an approval request (offboard, revoke and similar) may wait for a decision. A request that nobody decided in this time is closed as expired and can no longer be approved; the change must be requested again.
info.enabled: When set: requests raised from then on, and requests still waiting, expire after the number of hours you chose. PIM Manager applies the new value at once.
info.disabled: When blank or default: a request expires after 72 hours.
info.risk: A long time lets an old request be approved long after the reason for it was checked. A very short time makes requests expire before a second administrator has seen them, for example over a weekend. Reversible: set another value or go back to the default.
info.requires: SuperAdmin to change it. A whole number of hours from 1 to 720.
info.recommended: 72 hours. Raise it only if your approvers are regularly away longer than a weekend.

settings.label: A change to the emergency access list waits for its second SuperAdmin for at most (hours)
settings.where: Settings > Approvals & policy > Approval and request limits

info.what: A change to the list of emergency access (break-glass) accounts is requested by one SuperAdmin and approved by another. This is how long such a request may wait. After that it expires and can never be approved; it must be raised again.
info.enabled: When set: a request waits for the number of hours you chose. PIM Manager applies the new value at once, also to a request that is waiting.
info.disabled: When blank or default: a request waits for 72 hours.
info.risk: The emergency access list decides which accounts every guard leaves alone. A long wait lets a forgotten request be approved days later; the longest allowed is one week. A very short wait can make it impossible to get a second SuperAdmin in time. Reversible: set another value or go back to the default.
info.requires: SuperAdmin to change it. A whole number of hours from 1 to 168.
info.recommended: 72 hours.

settings.label: Longest extension a department owner may give (days)
settings.where: Settings > Approvals & policy > Approval and request limits

info.what: A department owner can move the end date of one of their people further into the future on the My people page. This is the furthest they may move it, counted in days from today. An earlier date is not an extension and keeps its own approval path.
info.enabled: When set: an extension beyond the number of days you chose is refused, with the limit in the message. PIM Manager applies the new value at once.
info.disabled: When blank or default: an owner may extend by up to 365 days.
info.risk: A high number lets an owner keep an account alive for years without anybody else looking at it. A low number means owners must extend more often. Reversible: set another value or go back to the default; dates already extended stay as they are.
info.requires: SuperAdmin to change it. A whole number of days from 1 to 3650.
info.recommended: 365 days or less, matching how often you want an owner to confirm that a person still needs access.

settings.label: Refuse to create a group that has no owner

info.what: When the engine creates a group in Microsoft Entra ID it looks for an owner: the owners or sponsor on the group's definition, or the contact of its department. This switch decides what happens when none of them resolves to a person.
info.enabled: When on: the engine does not create the group and reports the failure on Jobs, naming the group. The group is created on a later run once an owner is set.
info.disabled: When off (the default): the group is created without an owner and the run says so in a warning every time. An owner set later is attached by a later run without touching the group.
info.risk: On: a definition without an owner blocks its group, and everything that depends on the group, until someone fills the owner in -- on an estate where many definitions have no owner, most new groups will not be created. Off: groups can exist that nobody is responsible for. Reversible: switch it back; groups already created are not changed.
info.requires: SuperAdmin to change it. The engine reads it at its next run.
info.recommended: Off until your group definitions carry owners. Switch it on when you want every new group to have a responsible person from the start.

settings.label: Report a group as unused when nobody activated it for (days)

info.what: The validation reports a permission or role group that nobody has activated for a long time, or ever, so you can decide whether the access is still needed. This is the number of days without an activation after which a group is reported.
info.enabled: When set: a group is reported after the number of days you chose. The report is a note on the validation; nothing is removed and no commit is blocked.
info.disabled: When blank or default: a group is reported after 90 days without an activation.
info.risk: None for access: this only changes when a note appears. A low number produces many notes for groups that are used rarely on purpose; a high number hides access nobody uses. The check runs only when activation data for your groups has been read.
info.requires: SuperAdmin to change it. A whole number of days from 7 to 3650.
info.recommended: 90 days. Use a longer time if you have groups that are meant for rare tasks, such as a yearly audit.

settings.label: Sign-in methods an admin account must have (at least one of them)

info.what: The validation checks the sign-in methods registered on each admin account. An admin with none of the methods in this list is reported, and so is an admin who has only weak methods (text message, voice call, e-mail). The names are the method names Microsoft Entra ID uses.
info.enabled: When set: an admin must have at least one of the methods you listed. The report is a warning on the validation; no commit is blocked and no account is changed.
info.disabled: When blank or default: the list is the Microsoft Authenticator app, a passkey, a FIDO2 security key, Windows Hello for Business and a certificate.
info.risk: None for access: this only changes which admins get a warning. Taking strong methods out of the list produces warnings for admins who are well protected. Text message, voice call, phone and e-mail cannot be put in the list. Reversible: change the list or go back to the default.
info.requires: SuperAdmin to change it. Up to 12 method names, letters and digits only. The check runs only when the engine may read the sign-in methods of users and that data has been read.
info.recommended: The default list. Shorten it to passkey, fido2 and windowsHelloForBusiness if every admin must be phishing-resistant.

settings.label: Issue a Temporary Access Pass this long before its start time (hours)

info.what: For an admin account that asks for a Temporary Access Pass with a start time in the future, the engine waits until the start time is near before it issues and mails the pass. This is how many hours before the start time the pass is issued.
info.enabled: When set: a pass whose start time is further away than the number of hours you chose is left for a later run. With 0 the pass is issued only once its start time has come.
info.disabled: When blank or default: a pass is issued up to 48 hours before its start time.
info.risk: A pass is a sign-in credential in a mailbox. A long lead time means it sits there longer before it can be used; a short one leaves the new admin less time to find the mail before the first day. Reversible: set another value; passes already issued are not recalled.
info.requires: SuperAdmin to change it. A whole number of hours from 0 to 720. The engine reads it at its next run.
info.recommended: 48 hours.

settings.label: Issue a new Temporary Access Pass every time the last one ran out

info.what: Decides whether the engine issues a Temporary Access Pass once per admin account, or keeps issuing a new one whenever the previous pass has run out and the admin has still not completed their first sign-in.
info.enabled: When on: each time the last pass has expired the engine issues a new one and mails it, for as long as the admin row asks for a pass.
info.disabled: When off (the default): a pass is issued once. If the admin missed it, an administrator sends a new one with Reset TAP on the admin's row.
info.risk: On: a new sign-in credential is created and mailed again and again without anybody asking for it -- for an account nobody uses, this goes on until the row stops asking for a pass. Reversible: switch it off; passes already issued stay valid until they expire.
info.requires: SuperAdmin to change it. A mail sender must be set up. The engine reads it at its next run.
info.recommended: Off. Send a new pass on purpose with Reset TAP.

settings.label: Manage mail forwarding on the mailboxes of admin accounts

on.title: Forward admin mail to the person's normal mailbox?
on.body: When on, PIM Manager sends mail for admin accounts on to the mailbox you chose for each admin.
on.note: Note: it also removes forwarding that someone set up by hand on an admin mailbox, if PIM Manager wasn't asked for it.
more: Only admin accounts that have a mailbox are changed, and the mail is forwarded, not kept in the admin mailbox.
Mail for an admin account then lands in a normal mailbox, which is usually less protected.
If a permission is missing, PIM Manager says so once per run and changes nothing.
Switching it off later leaves forwarding as it is at that moment.

info.what: An admin row can ask for the mail sent to the admin account to be forwarded to the person's normal mailbox. This switch decides whether the engine sets that forwarding in Exchange Online when it creates or updates an admin account. Most admin accounts have no mailbox; for those nothing happens either way.
info.enabled: When on: for an admin account that has a mailbox, a row that asks for forwarding gets it (the mail is forwarded, not kept in the admin mailbox), and forwarding found on a mailbox whose row does not ask for it is cleared. A missing permission is reported once per run and changes nothing.
info.disabled: When off (the default): the engine never reads or changes mail forwarding.
info.risk: On: the engine changes mailbox settings in Exchange Online, and it clears forwarding that somebody set by hand on an admin mailbox when the row does not ask for it. Mail for a privileged account then lands in a normal mailbox, which is usually less protected. Reversible: switch it off; forwarding already set or cleared stays as it is.
info.requires: SuperAdmin to change it. The engine's identity needs permission to manage Exchange Online as an application, with an Exchange role that may change mailboxes. The engine reads the switch at its next run.
info.recommended: Off, unless your admin accounts have mailboxes and you want their mail to reach the person.

settings.label: Send a mail about newly discovered resources to

info.what: When the discovery sweep finds resources it has not seen before -- a new subscription, management group, resource group, workspace or role -- it records each in the audit trail. With an address here it also sends one mail per sweep that lists what is new.
info.enabled: When set: after a sweep that found something new, one mail with the list goes to the addresses you entered (several are separated by a semicolon).
info.disabled: When blank or default: no mail is sent. New resources are still recorded in the audit trail.
info.risk: The mail names resources in your tenant, so send it only to people who may know them. It follows your mail controls: a redirect or the mail kill switch applies to it too. Reversible: clear the field.
info.requires: SuperAdmin to change it. Up to 20 e-mail addresses. A mail sender must be set up, and the discovery sweep (a Pro feature) must be switched on under Settings > Features & edition. The engine reads it at its next run.
info.recommended: The mailbox of the team that decides what PIM Manager should manage.

settings.label: Read access requests from the ServiceNow drop store

info.what: Switches the ServiceNow intake on: the scheduled intake job reads the requests your ServiceNow integration has dropped for PIM Manager and turns each into a proposal.
info.enabled: When on: at its next run the intake job processes every request once. An accepted request becomes a proposal on Pending changes that an administrator reviews and commits; a rejected or unsupported one is marked with the reason. Nothing is applied to your tenant without a commit.
info.disabled: When off (the default): the intake job reports that the integration is not enabled and reads nothing. Requests already dropped stay where they are.
info.risk: On: people outside PIM Manager can put proposals into Pending changes. They still need an administrator's commit, but a busy administrator may commit a proposal without checking where it came from. Reversible: switch it off; proposals already created stay on Pending changes until committed or discarded.
info.requires: SuperAdmin to change it. Your ServiceNow integration must deliver the requests; the intake job must be enabled on Jobs.
info.recommended: Off unless you run the ServiceNow integration.

settings.label: Discovery: what happens with a newly discovered resource
settings.default: Report only, for every type of resource

on.title: Let PIM Manager act on new resources it finds?
on.body: With Stage for review a new resource waits for an administrator, and with Create automatically PIM Manager creates its group by itself.
on.note: Note: with Create automatically, groups appear without any administrator involved.

info.what: Per type of resource the discovery sweep can find -- an Azure subscription, a management group, a resource group, a Power BI workspace -- you choose what PIM Manager does with a new one: report it only, stage a group definition for your review, or queue the creation of its delegation group as a normal change.
info.enabled: When a type is set to 'Stage for review': a definition row for the new resource is staged on Pending changes and nothing happens until an administrator commits it. When set to 'Create automatically': the creation is queued as a change and the engine creates the group without a person committing it.
info.disabled: For a type left on 'Report only' (the default): a new resource is recorded in the audit trail. Nothing is staged or created.
info.risk: Create automatically means groups appear in Microsoft Entra ID because somebody created a resource -- for example a test subscription -- with no administrator involved. Stage for review keeps a person in the decision. Reversible: set the type back; groups already created stay.
info.requires: SuperAdmin to change it. Pro, and the discovery sweep switched on (Settings > Features & edition).
info.recommended: Report only, or Stage for review for the types you always want managed. Use Create automatically only where every new resource of that type must be governed from its first day.
